Perez's son, and the line that ends in David runs through him; Ruth closes with it and Matthew picks it up. The same name marks a spot on Judah's southern border, west of Kadesh-barnea.

Reuben's son, listed with the family that went down to Egypt and again in Reuben's line in Exodus and Chronicles. He is a different man from Perez's son of the same name.

Another of Benjamin's sons, whose descendants became one of the tribe's clans in the genealogies.

fb: The third camp after Sinai, in the wilderness of Paran. Miriam and Aaron challenged Moses here over his Cushite wife. Miriam was struck with a skin disease and healed when Moses prayed for her.

H2697.d: a Chetsronite or (collectively) descendants of Chetsron
fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Two clans in the wilderness census carried this name. One came from Reuben's son Hezron, the other from Judah's line through Perez, and that second one is David's own family.

fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Gilead's son, of Manasseh, and the father of Zelophehad. Zelophehad had five daughters and no son, and their case before Moses won daughters the right to inherit.
Named twice, in Joshua and 1 Kings, and nowhere else.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 4 men called Hepher. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A warrior from the divided-kingdom years, and 1 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

The border point near Kadesh-barnea on the south of the promised land, which Joshua 15:3 calls Addar.

H2674.d: Chatsor, the name (thus simply) of two places in Palestine and of one in Arabia
fb: The head of all the Canaanite kingdoms, in Joshua's words, and the biggest city-state in the region. Its fall decided the northern campaign. The dig there found a huge Bronze Age city to match.
Jeremiah 49 pronounces judgment on the kingdoms of Hazor and says the place will be left desolate for good. It is not Joshua's Canaanite city; the name also belonged to a place in Arabia.
Joshua names him once, and nothing else is recorded.
Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.
Nehemiah names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

H2675.d: new Chatsor, a place in Palestine
fb: It is new Hazor, Hazor-hadattah, in the far south near Moladah, and Joshua 15:25 is its only appearance.
One of the towns in the far south of Judah's allotment, near the border with Edom, and its site has not been found.
It lay on Zebulun's border in Galilee, and the Amarna letters of the fourteenth century BC already name it, as Hinnatuna, a garrison town fought over on the road through Galilee.
Issachar's town near Shunem in Joshua 19:19. El-Afuleh in the Jezreel Valley is the tentative match, on geography more than evidence.

Jeremiah's cousin. Babylon's army was round Jerusalem when Jeremiah bought Hanamel's field in Anathoth. He did it on purpose, as a sign that land would be bought and sold in Judah again.
